Copper Home User Guide
Meet Copper Home
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
2
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
1 Meet Copper Home
Copper Home is the desert-smart assistant for the whole household. It answers
questions, runs your smart home, remembers what matters, and keeps an eye on
the Arizona weather. Wake it by saying "Hey Copper."
1.1 What's in the box

Copper Home speaker

Power adapter with a 6-foot cable

Quick start card
1.2 Parts of your Copper Home

copper robot when Copper is listening

Copper Home comes in three fabric colors: Polished Copper, Patina Teal, and
Night Sky. It has no battery and must stay plugged in.

Copper Home User Guide
Set up Copper Home
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
3
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
2 Set up Copper Home
2.1 Before you start

The Copper app on an iPhone or Android phone

Your home Wi-Fi name and password (2.4 GHz or 5 GHz)

A spot within reach of an outlet, away from the sink and the stove
2.2 Setup steps
1
Plug in Copper Home. After a few seconds the light ring flashes blue: it's in
setup mode.
2
Open the Copper app and tap Add Device.
3
Choose Copper Home and follow the prompts.
4
Pick your Wi-Fi network and enter the password.
5
Name the room Copper Home is in, for example "Kitchen."
6
When the light ring turns soft white, say "Hey Copper, what's the weather?" to
test it.
NOTE The light ring flashing blue for more than 10 minutes means setup didn't finish.
Unplug Copper Home, plug it back in, and start again in the app.
2.3 Updates
Copper Home updates itself overnight when it's connected to Wi-Fi. To check your
version, open the Copper app and go to Devices > Copper Home > About. This
guide covers Copper 2.3.

Copper Home User Guide
Wi-Fi and connection
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
4
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
3 Wi-Fi and connection
Copper Home needs Wi-Fi for everyday questions, smart-home control, and
updates. Simple commands like timers keep working without it.
3.1 Reconnect to Wi-Fi or change networks
1
Open the Copper app.
2
Go to Devices > Copper Home > Wi-Fi.
3
Tap Change network.
4
Choose your network and enter the password. The light ring flashes blue while
Copper Home connects.
If you changed your router or your Wi-Fi password, do this right away. Copper
Home can't find the new network on its own.
3.2 Tips for a strong connection

Keep Copper Home within about 30 feet of your router, with few walls in
between.

Keep it off the floor and away from microwaves and metal cabinets.

If your router has separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks, the 2.4 GHz one
reaches farther.
NOTE Error C-12 means Copper Home lost its Wi-Fi connection or the password is
wrong. See page 9.

Copper Home User Guide
Talking to Copper
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
5
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
4 Talking to Copper
Say "Hey Copper" and then your request. The light ring turns Sonoran Sunset
orange while Copper listens. Copper understands English and Spanish.
4.1 Things to try
You say
What happens
"Hey Copper, set a timer for 10 minutes."
Handled on the device, even without
Wi-Fi
"Hey Copper, turn off the lights."
Handled on the device
"Hey Copper, what's the weather this weekend?"
Answered in the Copper Cloud
"Hey Copper, add milk to the list."
Added to your shopping list in the app
"Hey Copper, plan a 3-day Sedona trip for two
kids who hate hiking."
A complex request. With Copper Plus,
Copper uses Refined answers
4.2 Everyday answers and Refined answers
Most questions are answered by Raw Ore, Copper's everyday cloud model. With a
Copper Plus subscription, complex questions and planning get Refined answers
from more advanced models. Copper decides which to use for each request. See
the Copper Plus FAQ for details.
4.3 When Copper isn't sure
Since Copper 2.2, Copper says "I'm not sure" instead of guessing. Check important
information, like medical, legal, or money questions, with a trusted source.

Copper Home User Guide
Household Memory and privacy
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
7
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
6 Household Memory and privacy
6.1 Household Memory
Copper can remember things for the whole household. Say "Copper, remember
the pool guy comes Thursdays." Later, ask "When does the pool guy come?"

To forget something, say "Copper, forget the pool guy."

To see or delete every memory, open the Copper app and go to Memory.

Memories are kept for 30 days on the free plan and 12 months with Copper
Plus. You can delete them anytime.
6.2 What Copper hears and saves

Copper Home listens on the device for "Hey Copper." Nothing is sent to the
cloud until it hears the wake word.

After the wake word, your request (audio and text) is sent to the Copper Cloud
and saved: 30 days on the free plan, 12 months with Copper Plus.

You can review and delete your requests anytime in the Copper app under
Privacy > History.

Copper State Labs does not sell your recordings, and doesn't use them to train
models unless you opt in.
NOTE Want a break? Slide the mute switch on the back. The red privacy light means
the microphones are off.

Copper Home User Guide
Smart home and Arizona features
CSL-UG-0101-EN Rev. C
8
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
7 Smart home and Arizona features
7.1 Smart-home control
Copper Home controls lights, thermostats, sprinklers, and garage doors. Add them
in the Copper app under Devices > Add smart-home device. Some older
thermostats need their own app linked first; follow the prompts in the Copper app.
7.2 Arizona features
Feature
What it does
Monsoon Mode
Storm alerts, and automatically pauses your sprinklers when rain is
coming
Haboob Alert
Warns you about incoming dust storms and reminds you to close the
windows
Heat Check
Alerts you when it's dangerously hot, and reminds you to bring pets
inside and check the back seat before you leave the car
Snowbird Mode
Pauses your routines and checks in on the house while you're away
for the summer
Arizona time
Most of Arizona doesn't use daylight saving time, and Copper knows
it (fixed in Copper 2.1). The Navajo Nation does observe daylight
saving time
Turn features on or off in the Copper app under Devices > Copper Home >
Features.

When the light ring flashes red, Copper Home has a problem. The Copper app
shows an error code.
Code
What it means
What to do
C-12
Wi-Fi connection lost, or the
Wi-Fi password is wrong
Re-enter your Wi-Fi details in the Copper app
(page 4). Move Copper Home closer to the
router
C-47
Microphone array fault
Unplug Copper Home for 30 seconds, then
plug it back in. If C-47 keeps coming back,
contact the Copper Crew
C-90
Software update failed
Keep Copper Home connected to Wi-Fi and
retry the update in the Copper app
8.1 Common problems
Problem
Try this
Copper wakes up when the TV
is on
Something on TV sounded like "Hey Copper." Move
Copper Home farther from the TV, or slide the mute switch
during shows

Check for the red privacy light (muted). Make sure the light
ring isn't flashing red
Smart-home device not found
Make sure the device works in its own app, then add it
again in the Copper app
8.2 Factory reset
A factory reset erases your settings and returns Copper Home to setup mode. Hold
the volume-down button and the action button together for 15 seconds, until
the light ring flashes red three times. Then set it up again (page 3).

Copper Notes User Guide
Charging and battery
CSL-UG-0201-EN Rev. C
3
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
2 Charging and battery
Place Copper Notes on its charging puck, contacts down. The magnet lines it up.
Connect the puck to a USB-C power adapter with the included cable.
Battery fact
Value
Recording time
Up to 12 hours
Standby
Up to 7 days
Full charge
About 90 minutes
Low battery
Ring turns orange below 20%
2.1 Make it last a full day

A long conference day can use more than one full charge. Top up on the puck at
lunch: 20 minutes adds about 3 hours of recording.

Pause (double-tap) during breaks instead of leaving it recording.

Heat drains the battery. Keep Copper Notes out of direct sun.
IMPORTANT Never leave Copper Notes in a parked car or on a dashboard. It protects
itself from heat by shutting down (error C-63, page 8).

Copper Notes User Guide
Set up Copper Notes
CSL-UG-0201-EN Rev. C
4
© 2026 Copper State Labs, Inc. · Fictional company and documents, for educational use only.
3 Set up Copper Notes
1
Place Copper Notes on its charging puck.
2
Open the Copper app on your phone and tap Add Device.
3
Choose Copper Notes.
4
Hold the center button for 3 seconds, until the ring flashes green.
5
Follow the prompts to connect to your Wi-Fi.
3.1 Why Copper Notes needs Wi-Fi
Copper Notes records and transcribes without Wi-Fi. It uploads transcripts to the
Copper app the next time it's on Wi-Fi, usually while charging. If it can't upload for a
long time, its storage fills up (error C-31, page 8).
3.2 Change Wi-Fi networks
In the Copper app, go to Devices > Copper Notes > Wi-Fi and tap Change
network. Keep Copper Notes on its puck while it connects.
NOTE Error C-12 means Copper Notes can't reach Wi-Fi or the password is wrong.

When recording starts, Copper Notes plays the Consent Chime and lights the
amber ring so people know. You are responsible for following local
recording-consent laws. Some states require everyone in a conversation to agree
to being recorded. When in doubt, ask first.

5 Summaries and the Copper app
Copper Notes transcribes your recording on the device. Only the text goes to the
Copper Cloud to be summarized. When your summary is ready, the ring flashes
green briefly and the summary appears in the Copper app.
5.1 What you can do in the app

Read the summary, decisions, and action items

Read the full transcript with speaker labels ("who said what", added in Copper
2.3)

Share a summary by email or link

Delete a recording, transcript, or summary
NOTE Speaker labels are good, not perfect. Before you share a summary, check that
each decision is credited to the right person.

Q What is Copper Plus?
An optional subscription that gives your household smarter answers on Copper Home, longer
summaries and unlimited recording on Copper Notes, and a longer memory.
Q Do I need Copper Plus to use my device?
No. Every Copper device works on the free plan. Copper Plus adds features on top.

Refined answers and Copper Home
Q What are Refined answers?
Copper answers most questions with Raw Ore, an everyday cloud model that's quick and good for
most jobs. Refined uses more advanced models for complex questions and planning, like "Plan a
3-day Sedona trip for two kids who hate hiking" or "Explain my water bill." Refined is only available
with Copper Plus.
Q Does every question use Refined?
No. Copper picks the right model for each request. Simple commands run on the device, everyday
questions use Raw Ore, and complex requests use Refined. In a typical Copper Plus household,
about 1 in 5 requests gets a Refined answer.
Q Can I choose Refined for a question?
Copper chooses automatically. If an answer isn't detailed enough, ask a follow-up, like "Can you
go into more detail?"
Q What changes for Household Memory?
Memories are kept for 12 months instead of 30 days. You can still view and delete any memory
anytime in the Copper app.

Copper Plus and Copper Notes
Q How much can I record?
The free plan includes up to 10 hours of recording a month. Copper Plus has no monthly limit.
Q What's a long-form summary?
A detailed summary for long meetings and lectures, with sections, key points, decisions, and
action items. Standard summaries are shorter and cover the main points.
Q Can I search my old meetings?
Yes, with Copper Plus. Search across all your past recordings, for example "What did we decide
about the budget?" On the free plan you can read each summary, but not search across them.
Q Is my recording sent to the cloud?
Copper Notes transcribes on the device. Only the transcript goes to the Copper Cloud to be
summarized. With Copper Plus, transcripts and summaries are kept for 12 months instead of 30
days.

Billing, trials, and refunds
Q Is there a free trial?
Yes. Every new Copper device comes with a 30-day free trial of Copper Plus. Your subscription
starts automatically when the trial ends, unless you cancel before the last day.
Q Does one subscription cover all my devices?
Yes. One Copper Plus subscription covers every Copper device in your household, whether it's
one Copper Home or three Copper Homes and two Copper Notes.
Q How do I cancel?
In the Copper app, go to Settings > Subscription and tap Cancel. You keep Copper Plus until the
end of the period you've paid for.
Q Can I get a refund?
Monthly plans aren't refunded for partial months. Annual plans get a full refund if you cancel within
14 days of purchase. See Section 4 of the Terms and Conditions.
Q Can I switch between monthly and annual?
Yes. Switch in Settings > Subscription. The new plan starts at your next renewal. The annual plan
costs $79, less than 12 months at $7.99.

Privacy and is it worth it?
Q Does Copper record me?
Copper Home listens on the device for "Hey Copper" and sends nothing to the cloud until it hears
it. After the wake word, your request is saved: 30 days on the free plan, 12 months with Copper
Plus. You can delete it anytime in the Copper app.
Q What happens to my data if I cancel?
Your household goes back to the free plan, which keeps data for 30 days. Review anything you
want to keep before your paid period ends.
Q Do you sell my recordings or use them to train AI?
No. Copper State Labs doesn't sell recordings and doesn't use them to train models unless you
opt in.
Q Is Copper Plus worth it for me?
If you mostly use Copper Home for timers, lights, and the weather, the free plan may be all you
need. Copper Plus is worth it if you ask Copper complex questions, record more than 10 hours a
month on Copper Notes, or want your household's memories kept longer. Try it free for 30 days
and decide.
Q How do I get priority support?
Copper Plus members are first in line with the Copper Crew. Contact them in the Copper app
under Settings > Help.
